index: A: Thanks for being willing to give Walltaker a try! It's pretty easy to get started, but it might seem a bit weird at first since there are some hoops we have to jump through to be able to update your wallpaper.

Firstly, you will need an account. You can make an account by pressing the Sign Up link on the top-right-hand side of the screen. Once you have created an account (which should only take a minute) return to this page. You must be logged in to continue.

Now that you have an account, you should make a Link. The core "thing" in Walltaker is links. They are the sharable page that you can post on social media or give to friends that lets them change your wallpaper. In order to create your own link:

There are 8 options to change here that affect who can set your wallpaper, and what restrictions they have to work within. Set these as you see fit, using the key below to explain what each option does.

Your link terms are simply an area to express what you'd like to see as wallpapers more generally. Nothing here is enforced, it's just a text field for you to leave a note that appears on the link. I suggest you outline what things turn you on here.
Ensures that the link will never expire, and people you allow to set the link will be able to do so until you delete it.
This restricts who can set wallpapers on this link.
A list of E621 tags that must NOT appear on wallpapers people submit. Tags are separated by spaces or commas.

Theme tags are special! This is a way to enforce all wallpapers submitted to this link to be tagged with a single, specific tag of your choosing. Use this when you're looking for something specific, like a specific species or sex act. You're horny, you'll come up with something fun. Be careful about how you type your tag in here. If you misspell this theme tag, no one will be able to submit anything until you remove it or correct the spelling. Confirm spelling on E621 if you have to. Filter tags cannot be used.
When you've set it up how you'd like, click the Create Link button.

Congratulations! You should have a fresh link ready to share with the world. However, it currently doesn't change the wallpaper on anything. This is because, as simply a website, Walltaker cannot change your wallpaper for you. To allow us to do this, we need a Walltaker Client, which is an app you can install on which ever devices you'd like to get wallpaper updates on. It will silently check your link every few seconds, and update your wallpaper if there's someone has updated your wallpaper, automatically.
You can download a client for which ever device you'd like to use. Follow the instructions for each one for how to install it, then return to this tutorial.
Once you've installed your client, you need to configure it to pull wallpapers from specifically YOUR link. You can do this by going to your link page, and getting the link ID.
Follow the instructions for your client to add this link to it. Normally it's in a menu where you can simply type in the link ID.
Wow! You have everything set up now! Let's just verify that everything is working, and then you can share your link publicly!

Your client pinged this link at least once, but gave up! This could be due to a number of things: Did your client crash? Some phone operating systems kill background apps, this can sometimes affect clients. Refer to client documentation. Did you change the frequency of checks? client_guide: Older polling clients still work for now.
You can also pass a client identifier during subscription, however this will only appear if a site admin adds your client to the list.

The JavaScript example uses the Action Cable client. Python and C++ connect directly and read the payload from the Action Cable envelope's message field; ignore control frames such as welcomes, pings, and subscription confirmations. The setWallpaper / set_wallpaper function is where your client downloads and applies the wallpaper.

Native clients may also identify themselves with WebSocket handshake headers such as User-Agent , joihow , User_Agent , or Wallpaper-Engine-Client . Browser WebSocket clients usually cannot set custom handshake headers, so use subscription params or announce_client .

The server sends this payload immediately after subscribing and every time client-visible link state changes. Treat post_url as the current wallpaper URL. If that request is rejected by the e621 CDN, clients can retry with post_url_backup , a Walltaker-hosted URL that supplies the CDN's required request headers. The backup is null when the primary URL is not a supported e621 media URL. The token below is a placeholder; use the complete backup URL received from the server. Users can enable videos and GIFs on some links, so clients should handle file types they cannot display. post_url can also be null if no wallpaper is set.

Link updates always include the fields above. set_by is a username or null ; response_type and response_text may be null before a reaction is sent. post_description is the full description in WebSocket updates. Presence and reaction changes also trigger updates, so download the wallpaper only when post_url changes.
If the link does not exist, the channel sends an error payload and does not stream link updates.
Set a response for a given link. There are 4 kinds of responses.
🔑 Requires the link owner's API key. Use the numeric id from the link payload in this endpoint.
⚠️ A disgust response rolls the wallpaper back to the previous image and sends the changed state over the WebSocket. If no previous image exists, post_url and post_thumbnail_url become null .

A successful request returns HTTP 200 and the link JSON below. Unlike a WebSocket link update, this response has no success field. set_by is omitted when no setter is recorded, and post_description is omitted when blank or truncated to 100 characters when present. An invalid API key returns 403 , an invalid reaction type returns 400 , and a missing link returns 404 ; these errors contain a message field.
🔓/🔐 API key required for some, but not all data.

ℹ️ The links array contains public, unexpired (or never-expiring) links. Each entry excludes success and set_by ; post_description is omitted when blank and truncated to 100 characters when present. friend and self are included only when an API key or browser session authenticates the viewer. The legacy field master contains the owner's username, or false if no owner is set.
Call watch_user again with a new username when the wallpaper is set by someone else.

Replace polling GET /api/links/[id].json with one long-lived LinkChannel subscription. The WebSocket message payload intentionally matches the link JSON shape, so most wallpaper update code can keep using post_url , post_url_backup , post_thumbnail_url , set_by , and updated_at .
